LOC_001: This is North Classroom Building, Room 2010. It contains two faculty offices and a shared common area used by teaching assistants (TAs). Room 2010A is the office of Moatassem Abdallah, Associate Professor in Civil Engineering at CU Denver and Co-founder & CEO of Commutrics. His research focuses on sustainability of buildings and infrastructure systems using operations research and decision analytics, including infrastructure maintenance, transportation behavior, V2G energy optimization, and construction planning. He has secured approximately $3M in research funding from the NSF and state agencies and teaches courses in construction planning, BIM, construction management, and engineering systems. Room 2010B is the office of Caroline Clevenger, Professor in Construction Engineering & Management at CU Denver. Her work focuses on Building Information Modeling (BIM), virtual design & construction (VDC), sustainable building systems, lifecycle performance, and digital technologies in construction. She teaches undergraduate and graduate courses in BIM, construction management, and project delivery systems.
LOC_002: This is North Classroom Building, Room 2506. It serves as the main office space for the Department of Civil Engineering and contains three offices. Room 2506A is the office of Pam Metler, Program Manager for the Civil Engineering Program, who oversees program operations, coordination, and administrative support. Room 2506B is the office of Aana Rase, Program Coordinator, who supports academic scheduling, student services, and departmental coordination. Room 2506C is the office of Liv Lindenberg, Program Manager for the Construction Engineering and Management Program, who manages program administration, student support, and coordination for CEM programs.
LOC_003: This is North Classroom Building, Room 2502. It is the office of Kevin L. Rens, Professor and Chair of the Department of Civil Engineering at CU Denver and Founding Director of the Construction Engineering Management program. He holds a PhD, PE (Professional Engineer), and F.ASCE (Fellow of the American Society of Civil Engineers). He is a Past Chair of the Forensic Engineering Division and a Life Member of the National Society of Black Engineers. His expertise covers repair, evaluation, maintenance, and rehabilitation of civil infrastructure including dams, buildings, bridges, and streets. He has been a faculty member at UCD since 1995, teaches graduate and undergraduate courses in structural mechanics, analysis, and design, and leads departmental strategy, accreditation, and industry engagement.
